title: Two missionary brothers
hook: a nun who never leaves her convent becomes a sister to two young men across the world, and the week comes back
tomorrow: after everything, what were Thérèse's last words?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Thérèse guiding the novices, wanting to help them more than to be liked. Your line was honest and kind. Today the week comes back, with one more piece.

A friend on deployment. A cousin on a mission trip you text at strange hours because of the time zones. A pen pal you've never seen in person. Every message says the same small thing: you're still mine, even from here. Thérèse never left her convent. And yet, in Manuscript C, she writes about a joy she had wanted for a long time: a brother. A young man training for the priesthood asked the Carmel for a sister who would pray for him, and the request was handed to her.
screen: `TEXTS ACROSS TIME ZONES.` → `A JOY SHE WANTED: A BROTHER.` → `THE REQUEST COMES TO HER.`

segments.voice: Later a second one came, a young priest leaving as a missionary. She hesitated. Her prayers were already offered for the first; could she split them? She decides she can't divide what belongs to Jesus, and gives it all to both. She writes to them as a sister: encouragement, honesty, her little way, sent across the world from inside walls she won't leave. Prayer was the one thing she could send anywhere, and she sent all of it. Near the end of the manuscript she takes a line from the Song of Songs, in the Douay-Rheims: "Draw me: we will run after thee." When one soul is drawn to God, she says, the souls it loves come running behind. Now look back at the week, because every piece was in it. The cross first, waiting just inside the convent door at fifteen. The holy face, seen in her father's hidden years of illness. The smile, for the sister who grated. A little splash, at the washing tub. Petals, the small sacrifices thrown where nobody saw. Honest and kind, with the novices. And now a sister far away: love that crosses an ocean without moving.
screen: `A SECOND BROTHER.` · `ONE PRAYER, NOT DIVIDED.` · `DRAW ME: WE WILL RUN.` · `SIX LINES FROM THIS WEEK.` · then, large: `A SISTER FAR AWAY.`

segments.voice: Count on your fingers the people far from you who carry you somehow: someone who prays for you, writes to you, thinks of you when you don't know it. One finger each, and a name for every finger. Then let the sit hold all of them at once.
Two missionary brothers. The young men Thérèse wrote to as a sister, from a convent she never left.
Your line: a sister far away. Distance doesn't cancel being family. Have a good week.

howItsDone: Some Catholics, especially in religious communities, commit to praying for a particular priest or missionary for years, and the Church honors Thérèse as a patron of missions.

notes: Paraphrased from Manuscript C; confirm: a seminarian asked Carmel for a sister to pray for him and the request was given to Thérèse; she had long desired a brother priest; a second, a missionary priest, was given to her later; she hesitated and then decided not to divide; she reads 'Draw me, we will run' as souls running after the one drawn. The index says 'two young priests'; the first was a seminarian when the request came. The hook says 'training for the priesthood'. Roulland met Thérèse once in the convent parlor, so the script avoids saying she never met them.
